paras: The killing of John Hill was the fatal shooting of a Black passenger by Deputy Sheriff J. P. Brents on a Southern Railway passenger train near Coalburg, Alabama, on the night of 14 August 1905. The deputy said Hill had twice reached toward his pocket while being arrested, and officers called the shooting self-defense.

The Birmingham Age-Herald placed the shooting about 11 o'clock Monday night between Birmingham and Republic; the Montgomery Advertiser put it near Coalburg. Brents was riding the train to Republic when the conductor asked him to go into the "negro car" and arrest a "boisterous negro," warning him of the man's "dangerous character." The Advertiser added that the man had been picking a quarrel with other Black passengers.

In the version drawn from the deputy's statement and unnamed eyewitnesses, Hill raised his hands when ordered, then tried to put a hand in his hip pocket. When he did not obey a second order and made another move, Brents fired twice with a .45 calibre Colt revolver and killed him instantly. The Advertiser told it slightly differently: Hill withdrew his hand on seeing the deputy's pistol and reached again only after the officer had put the weapon away. Neither paper reports that a weapon was found on Hill.
The Age-Herald reported that the shooting was "being carefully investigated" but that officers believed it was in self-defense. No report of an inquest or grand jury action appears in the coverage.

Coverage was limited to two Alabama papers on 16 August. The Age-Herald ran the story under the headline "Negro Man Killed by Deputy Brents," with a deck stating as fact that he "attempted to draw weapon while under arrest." The Advertiser's brief item, "Negro Shot on Train," gave the victim's name only as "supposed to be John Hill" and described his movements without attribution. Both papers relied on the officer's side of the story, and no Black-press report of the shooting was found.
The local Age-Herald's "Monday night" gives 14 August, while the Advertiser's "last night" in its 16 August issue would point to 15 August.

reader.title: Killing of John Hill
bases: A deputy sheriff shot and killed a Black passenger he had been asked to arrest on a train, with no crowd involved (A1, A2).
Two Alabama papers independently report the killing with differing details (A1, A2), though both justifications rest on the deputy's own statement and unnamed witnesses (A2).

accounts.label: Deputy's statement (Age-Herald)
accounts.gist: Hill obeyed an order to raise his hands, then reached for his hip pocket; after a second command he again tried to draw a weapon and the deputy fired twice.

accounts.label: Advertiser report
accounts.gist: Hill offered resistance and reached for his rear pocket, withdrew his hand when the deputy showed a pistol, then reached again after the deputy put the pistol away, and was shot twice.

framing.detail: The Age-Herald headline 'Attempted to Draw Weapon While Under Arrest' states the deputy's claim as fact and closes with officers' belief in self-defense.
The Advertiser's short item calls Hill 'boisterous' and describes his moves to his pocket without attribution.

sources.note: 'Negro Shot on Train': Deputy Sheriff J. P. Brentz killed a Black man 'supposed to be John Hill' on a Southern Railway passenger train near Coalburg; deputy's version of two moves to a pocket.
quotes: The negro was boisterous on the train and picking a quarrel with other negro passengers when the conductor informed Deputy Sheriff Brentz, who happened to be going to Republic.
Deputy Sheriff Brentz pulled his gun rapidly and fired two shots at the negro, killing him almost instantly.
